info.description:
# napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing) [![napari hub](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://api.napari-hub.org/shields/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing)](https://napari-hub.org/plugins/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing) [![tests](https://github.com/uderhardtlab/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/uderhardtlab/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![License: BSD-3-Clause](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSD_3--Clause-blue.svg)](https://github.com/uderhardtlab/napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing/blob/main/LICENSE) napari plugin and batch runner for light-sheet data of mouse peritoneum. It does three things: - finds the **outer surface of the muscle layer** from the TOM20 channel; - builds a **CD34 fibroblast mask**; - keeps only the CD34 above the muscle (the **submesothelial fibroblasts**) and exports binary TIFFs, e.g. for Imaris or as input for MASKEL. The algorithms are in `napari_maskel_ibex_preprocessing.core` and use only numpy/scipy (no napari). Both the napari widget and the command-line runner use them. ## Installation Into an existing napari environment (Python ≥ 3.9), either in napari via *Plugins > Install/Uninstall Plugins*, or: ``` pip install napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing ``` Use `pip install "napari-maskel-ibex-preprocessing[napari]"` to install napari as well. For development, from a clone of this repository: ``` pip install -e ".[testing]" pytest tests ``` ## Input A converted `.h5` file with one dataset per channel, `Channel_0`, `Channel_1`, …, each `(Z, Y, X)`. `Channel_0` carries the attribute `element_size_um` (voxel size `(dz, dy, dx)` in µm). An Imaris `.ims` file can be converted with `maskel-ibex-ims2h5 sample.ims`, or by the batch runner automatically. Assumed geometry: - the tissue is imaged en face, with the **mesothelium at high z** and the muscle at low z; - muscle is present under the whole field of view; - the fibres are roughly parallel. ## napari 1. Open the `.h5` (*File > Open*; choose this plugin's reader if asked). Every channel becomes an image layer with the correct voxel size. 2. Open *Plugins > MASKEL IBEX preprocessing > Muscle surface and CD34 filtering*. 3. Choose the **muscle channel** (TOM20) and the **CD34 channel**. For files from the reader, Channel_0 and Channel_3 are pre-selected. 4. For fast tuning, draw a **rectangle** in a Shapes layer (2D view) and choose that layer as the *region*. Every step has *Run on region* (seconds to a minute) and *Run on full volume* (minutes). Both run in the background. - **1 Muscle surface:** muscle mask, surface, height map `h` and the **signed distance map** `d = (z − h)·dz` (µm; > 0 = mesothelium side). - **2 CD34 mask:** CD34 mask, thresholded by hysteresis with a local, noise-based low threshold. - **3 Distance filter:** keeps CD34 components ≥ the minimum volume, then the part with `d >` cutoff → **fibroblast mask**. 5. **Export** (needs the full-volume results; TIFFs in the original image shape, uint8 0/255, voxel size in the metadata, optional ZIP compression): - *distance mask*: 1 where `d >` threshold (given in µm or in z slices), else 0; - *fibroblast mask*; - optionally all results as a steps `.h5`. Results computed on a region use Otsu thresholds and noise statistics of that region only. They can therefore differ slightly from the same area of a full-volume run. ## Batch ``` maskel-ibex-batch D:\data\sample.ims maskel-ibex-batch D:\data\round1 --dry-run maskel-ibex-batch D:\data\round1 --dist-threshold -4 --dist-unit um ``` - **Input:** a file or a folder. A folder means every `.h5` / `.ims` in it. - **Parameters:** the defaults below. - **Output per sample:** - `_layers.h5`, `_cd34.h5`, `_submeso_cd34.h5`: intermediate steps; - `_tif\…_fibroblast_mask.tif` and `…_distance_gt.tif`; - a log file. - `--force` recomputes, `--uncompressed` writes plain TIFFs. ## Steps and default parameters (`core/params.py`) | Step | Operation | Default | |---|---|---| | 1 | TOM20 block means (valid pixels only) | 4 × 4 px | | 1 | normalized Gaussian | σ (2, 5, 5) µm | | 1 | muscle = above the lowest 3-class multi-Otsu threshold; small objects removed | < 5000 µm³ | | 1 | fibre filter: binary opening with a line along the measured fibre direction (structure tensor) | 30 µm | | 1 | `h` = highest muscle z; empty columns from the nearest column; grey closing | disk 9.2 µm | | 2 | tissue = Otsu on log of the summed channels (2 × 2 blocks) | smoothing 5 µm | | 2 | CD34 normalized Gaussian minus background | σ (1, 0.5, 0.5) µm; background 15 µm | | 2 | seeds = above Otsu within tissue | | | 2 | noise = tissue outside the Otsu mask, in the band −10 ≤ d ≤ 30 µm; per block median + k · robust SD | blocks 272 µm, k = 4 | | 2 | hysteresis: components of the low-threshold mask that contain a seed; small objects removed | < 20 µm³ | | 3 | 26-connected components of the whole CD34 mask; keep those ≥ the minimum volume, then `d >` cutoff | 500 µm³; −4 µm | The defaults were validated on `LSM 2026-07-20_B6-12w-naive_co1-s1-r1` (naive, round 1). ## Development and releases - **Every push and pull request:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs the tests on Windows, Linux and macOS with Python 3.9–3.12. It also builds the package and checks it with `twine check`. - **Release:** set the new `version` in `pyproject.toml` and in `src/napari_maskel_ibex_preprocessing/__init__.py`, commit, then push a tag with the same version: ``` git tag v0.1.0 git push origin v0.1.0 ``` `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the package, checks that the tag matches the version, and publishes to PyPI through trusted publishing.
